topics.title: Mass Point Geometry Question
topics.text:
This is about the 2013 AMC 10B Problem 16.



In triangle $ABC$, medians $AD$ and $CE$ intersect at $P$, $PE=1.5$, $PD=2$, and $DE=2.5$. What is the area of $AEDC$?



$\qquad\textbf{(A)}13\qquad\textbf{(B)}13.5\qquad\textbf{(C)}14\qquad\textbf{(D)}14.5\qquad\textbf{(E)}15$ IMAGE



The Aops Wiki presents this solution:



Let us use mass points: Assign $B$ mass $1$. Thus, because $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$, $A$ also has a mass of $1$. Similarly, $C$ has a mass of $1$.  $D$ and $E$ each have a mass of $2$ because they are between $B$ and $C$ and $A$ and $B$ respectively. Note that the mass of $D$ is twice the mass of $A$, so AP must be twice as long as $PD$. PD has length $2$, so $AP$ has length $4$ and $AD$ has length $6$. Similarly, $CP$ is twice $PE$ and $PE=1.5$, so $CP=3$ and $CE=4.5$. Now note that triangle $PED$ is a $3-4-5$ right triangle with the right angle $DPE$. Since the diagonals of quadrilaterals $AEDC$, $AD$ and $CE$, are perpendicular, the area of $AEDC$ is $\frac{6 \times 4.5}{2}=\boxed{\textbf{(B)} 13.5}$



I am confused as to why the mass of B should not be split along BC and BA, considering that B is a lone point on the side of transversal DE. The solution says the mass of B is 1 along BC and BA, so I am a little confused. Thanks!

I was working on some past Sprint round and other tests when I stumbled upon questions like this:



There is a 2x2 square in a plane, and around it, integers are written, starting from one and going around clockwise while increasing. What number will be 15 squares to the left of square number 3?
